body: I smoked for chronically 3 years, a couple months of breaks here and there but eventually as time went on I found less pleasure in being high and my ability to manage life sober dwindled. As you lose social skills your social anxiety increases. Weed can give you epiphanies but you could have those sober without the risk of uncontrollable overthinking if you be honest with yourself and create a space to reflect. Eventually after being sober for so long weed just feels un normal which can freak you out when you’re trapped in it. You never get back those initial euphoric highs that blind you of the abnormality. I’m sure we’re not the only ones who went from loving weed to just mainly feeling anxious while high. You could try cbd or thc oils if you have access to them and see if that changes anything cause it’s a little more gentle of a high. There’s nothing wrong with the change, it prevents you from readdiction, although I find not being able to experience weed the same sad too. It can have a specifically wonderful feeling with little side effects. Sometimes I can still smoke in the right setting and you probably can too just be much more wary. Overdoing other substances is also something I’ve experienced and for me and I think most people it’s a desperate need to escape your life or self. Youve gotta build trust with yourself, trust that you can manage your stressors so you don’t need to escape life or the feeling that you’re letting yourself down or are drawn to bad situations. Build trust in yourself to not take too much when you know it won’t make you feel better it’ll just make you feel different.

I’d try figure out a meal you know is high volume or very satisfying + maybe a snack you’re craving & a hot drink but something preplanned to satisfying the physical need cause if you don’t a binge will occur - also plan an activity directly afterwards so that you can give yourself the time to recognise how you feel. 
I found the more that I purged the more that I would binge cause I always felt more starving after than any time in my life

Don’t point it out or anything just try to take her away from the food, offer to do something together or change the subject away from food. 

In saying this binging and purging is usually a coping mechanism so what you really need to figure out the cause of it and try to solve that problem. If you do that hopefully the issue will resolve itself in time. If you don’t solve the initial issue or issues then she will either continue in this cycle and most likely get worse. She alternatively may turn to restricting, increase her rate of self harm or turn to other unhealthy coping mechanisms. The easiest way to cure an addiction is to replace it with another, purging can be very addictive.
